## Solution

A 3×5 rectangle of toothpicks has 4 horizontal lines × 5 = 20 horizontal toothpicks, and 6 vertical lines × 3 = 18 vertical toothpicks, totaling 38. ✓

**Model.** Place vertices at grid points $(i,j)$ with $i=0,\dots,5$ and $j=0,\dots,3$. Each toothpick has unit length and burns in 10 s, so the flame speed is $1/10$ per second. Two adjacent corners are lit at time $0$; by symmetry take them to be $(0,0)$ and $(5,0)$.

**Time fire reaches each vertex.** Fire reaches a vertex via the shortest path (in edge count) from either source, multiplied by 10. The Manhattan distance from $(0,0)$ to $(i,j)$ is $i+j$, and from $(5,0)$ is $(5-i)+j$. Hence

$$T(i,j)=10\bigl(j+\min(i,\,5-i)\bigr).$$

Tabulating ($\min(i,5-i)$ equals $0,1,2,2,1,0$ for $i=0,\dots,5$):

| $j\backslash i$ | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 10 | 20 | 20 | 10 | 0 |
| 1 | 10 | 20 | 30 | 30 | 20 | 10 |
| 2 | 20 | 30 | 40 | 40 | 30 | 20 |
| 3 | 30 | 40 | 50 | 50 | 40 | 30 |

**When a toothpick is fully consumed.** If fire reaches its two ends at times $t_1\le t_2$:
- if $t_2-t_1\ge 10$: the earlier flame burns it entirely, finishing at $t_1+10$;
- if $t_2-t_1<10$: both flames advance and meet in the middle, finishing at $\frac{t_1+t_2+10}{2}$.

**Find the latest-finishing toothpick.** For every edge, compute its finish time from the two endpoint times above. The largest vertex times are $50$ s, attained only at $(2,3)$ and $(3,3)$. The edge joining them — the top-middle horizontal toothpick — has $t_1=t_2=50$, so it finishes at

$$\frac{50+50+10}{2}=55\text{ s}.$$

Every other edge has at least one endpoint $\le 40$:
- an edge with endpoints $(50,40)$ finishes at $\frac{50+40+10}{2}=50$ s;
- edges lower in the grid finish even earlier.

So no toothpick finishes later than $55$ s, and the top-middle toothpick achieves exactly $55$ s.

**Answer: the entire structure burns in $\boxed{55}$ seconds.**
